title: Proper ambient projection part of the product interchange grid
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring and let d1,d2 be two proper/open interchange diagrams for f:X→Y and g:Y→Z [def-pur-etale-graph-interchange-data]. Choose a side n and write m for the other side. Let F,G,H be their pairwise product presentations [lem-pur-etale-pairwise-product-graph-normalization, lem-pur-etale-graph-product-geometry]. For each presentation take its selected supporting neighborhood O_f=F.P×_{V_n}W_n, O_g=G.P×_{T_n}Y, O_h=H.P×_{P_n}W_n. Put barF=(z_f,j_f,F.p), barG=(z_g,j_g,G.p), barH=(z_h,j_h,H.p), where j is the open neighborhood inclusion and z is the product graph followed by the open inclusion of the intersection. Define a_f,a_g,a_h by the proper compositor splitting z q=a_n, the Cartesian proper/open side exchange, and the proper compositor for the ambient projection. No inverse graph triangle is included. Let N=H.P×_{P_n}V_n with open K:N→H.P, E:O_h→N induced by e_n, proper R:N→O_g induced by productP and r_n, and proper maps BV:F.P→N and BW:O_f→O_h induced by the product projections and k_m. Their B square commutes and their Q square (K,R,productP,j_g) commutes. Define barI by the inverse normalized B exchange and the normalized Q exchange, including the proper and open compositors, exactly as productInterchange [def-pur-etale-graph-product-interchange]. Then I_n;a_h=(a_f whiskered by G_n);(a_g whiskered by barF);barI. This equality contains only the proper ambient factors and no graph shrinking triangle.

proof.text: Use the source-lift subgrid to express the identity-normalized source transport as the f-side ambientLambda, the middle graph splitter, and the inverse B lift.
Use the target-square subgrid to replace rawSquare followed by the composite ambientLambda with sourceTransport followed by middleTail and squareInterchange.

Evaluate the isomorphism equalities on each input object. Apply the target-square equality, combine the two maps under the final functor, substitute the source-lift equality, and move the middleTail across the inverse B lift using its naturality. The associators and unitors have identity components. This gives exactly the unchanged selected-side equality, for each Boolean side.

lean.statement: theorem etaleGraphProductAmbientPasting (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A] {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z} (d₁ d₂ : EtaleGraphInterchangeDiagram f g) (second : Bool) : (match second with | false => let af := EtaleGraphPresentation.ProductRow.ambientLambda d₁.sourcePresentation d₂.sourcePresentation false A let ag := EtaleGraphPresentation.ProductRow.ambientLambda (EtaleGraphPresentation.ofCompactification d₁.compactification) (EtaleGraphPresentation.ofCompactification d₂.compactification) false A let ah := EtaleGraphPresentation.ProductRow.ambientLambda d₁.compositePresentation d₂.compositePresentation false A (etaleGraphDiagramInterchange A d₁).hom ≫ ah.hom = Functor.whiskerRight af.hom ((EtaleGraphPresentation.ofCompactification d₁.compactification).functor A) ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft ((EtaleGraphInterchangeDiagram.ProductRow.First.F d₁ d₂).functor A) ag.hom ≫ (EtaleGraphInterchangeDiagram.ProductRow.First.interchange d₁ d₂ A).hom | true => let af := EtaleGraphPresentation.ProductRow.ambientLambda d₁.sourcePresentation d₂.sourcePresentation true A let ag := EtaleGraphPresentation.ProductRow.ambientLambda (EtaleGraphPresentation.ofCompactification d₁.compactification) (EtaleGraphPresentation.ofCompactification d₂.compactification) true A let ah := EtaleGraphPresentation.ProductRow.ambientLambda d₁.compositePresentation d₂.compositePresentation true A (etaleGraphDiagramInterchange A d₂).hom ≫ ah.hom = Functor.whiskerRight af.hom ((EtaleGraphPresentation.ofCompactification d₂.compactification).functor A) ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft ((EtaleGraphInterchangeDiagram.ProductRow.Second.F d₁ d₂).functor A) ag.hom ≫ (EtaleGraphInterchangeDiagram.ProductRow.Second.interchange d₁ d₂ A).hom )
